abstract: Non-aqueous lithium-oxygen (Li–O2) batteries represent promising next-generation energy storage systems owing to their ultrahigh theoretical <mark>energy density</mark>. However, the electrically insulating discharge product of Li2O2 causes severe pore clogging and high charge overpotentials, severely restricting their practical implementation. Herein, a three-dimensional (3D) printed graphene aerogel cathode is fabricated via direct ink writing (DIW). When coupled with a CoBr2 redox mediator (RM), the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics are remarkably accelerated. …
